DILG BACONC P'UPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph OPINION NO. JUL 03 2024 HON. JULIUS FRAGO Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Maigo Lanao del Norte Julius.frago@qmail.com Dear SB Member Frago: This has reference to your electronic mail dated May 10, 2024, requesting this Department's opinion conceming the dismissal of a purok president after participating as an affiant to an election-related case, particularly the 2023 Synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (SBKE). As represented, the complaint was filed by the losing Punong Barangay candidate. Ostensibly, the concerned purok president is a staunch supporter and neighbor of the losing Punong Barangay candidate. It is your view that purok presidents' involvement could create conflict of interest within her purok and potentially undermine public trust. Hence, the subject query. Central to the resolution of the issue at hand is an understanding of the nature of a purok. In local parlance, a purok refers to a geographical zone or division within a barangay. It serves as a means to deliver basic services within a barangay, aimed at strengthening participatory govemance and more efficient public service delivery at the grassroots level. 1 Parenthetically, purok presidents are generally elected by the community or the residents of the purok and subsequently act as a representative or a leader for the community. Generally, they assist the barangay officials in implementing govemment basic services and programs and in managing community-related issues and concems. Having laid down the foregoing, it is important to note that the role and functions of purok presidents are not explicitly delineated in the law; rather, they are generally defined in local ordinances. Along this line, it is equally important to note that puroks are not officially regarded as a local govemment unit (LGU) under the Local Govemment Code (Republic Act 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code). At any rate, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 50, Series of 2022, we opined that a purok may be created or formally recognized by the barangay through a local ordinance. Pertinent portion thereof is worth quoting at length, thus: 1 DILG Legal Opinion No. 50, Series Of 2022, dated June 10, 2022 "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

"A purok may be created or formally recognized by the barangay through a local ordinance which may specify its metes and bounds, organization structure, internal rules, among others. This is allowed under the [Code] which provides that: "Section 387. Chief Officials and Offices. - (a) There shall be in each barangay a punong barangay, seven (7) sangguniang barangay members, the sangguniang kabataan chairman, a barangay secretary, and a barangay treasurer. (b) There shall also be in every barangay a lupong tagapamayapa. The sangguniang barangay may form community brigades and create such other positions or offices as may be deemed necessary to carry out the purposes of the barangay government in accordance with the needs of public service, subject to the budgetary limitations on personal services prescribed under Title Five, Book II of this Code." "Section 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. — (b) For efficient, effective and economical govemance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the punong barangay shall: (5) Upon approval by a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay, appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials. "Section 396. Other Appointive Officials. - The qualifications, duties, and functions of all other barangay officials appointed by the punong barangay shall be governed by the provisions of this Code and other laws or by barangay ordinances." In such instance, the purok shall subject to the LGC which, per the foregoing provisions, can be summarized that: (1) the members of the purok would belong to other appointive officials; (2) their appointments need the approval of the majority of all members of the sangguniang barangay; and (3) their qualifications, duties and functions shall be governed by a barangay ordinance. Formally established puroks are under the control and supervision of the barangay. particularly the ordinance creatinq or recoqnizinq the same. We nonetheless acknowledge that individuals may form clusters within themselves for purposes of, among others, efficiency and identification within their own barangay. The 1987 Constitution encourages non-governmental, community-based, and sectoral organizations that promote the welfare of the nation. Filipinos are also known to embody the spirit of bayanihan and organize themselves for the common interest of their community. In this regard, the organization may refer to itself, informally, as a purok or other nomenclatures such as a 'neighborhood association'. Private individuals who create their own group are allowed to set the rules and internal structure of their organization. Corollary thereto, the Barangay LGU, under the premise of advancing the general welfare of its constituents, may establish, acknowledge or Page 2 of 3

institutionalize their organizational existence through an ordinance." (Emphasis ours) Premised from the foregoing, we qualify our opinion—if the purok president is appointed by the Punong Barangay pursuant to an ordinance duly enacted by the sanggunian and in accordance with the above-cited provisions of the Code, then the ordinance should govem the purok president's term of office and grounds for dismissal. In the absence of such an ordinance, it is within the discretion of the Punong Barangay whether to retain or replace the purok president. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: Unde OUSEL VICT R. LLAMAS ry for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affai DIR. WILHELM M. SUYKO, CESO Regional Director, DILG-X (Northern Mindanao) Masterson Ave., Km. 8, Upper Carmen de Oro City Page 3 of 3
